analysis.title: GS Pasquariello - markets / macro :: five short points. 12 Oct 2026
key_insights: Pasquariello argues US equity breadth is better than reported. The median S&P stock is 15% below its 52-week high, the worst reading since the dot-com bubble. Even so, S&P, NDX, RTY and SPW are up double digits YTD (the Dow is the exception), all but two S&P sectors are higher on the year, and nearly 2-in-3 S&P names are positive.

Dispersion is wide on the upside. 123 S&P names are up 25% or more versus 42 down 25% or more, and 53 are up 50% or more versus 8 down 50% or more. The desk calls it a bifurcated market but says returns within it are better than many give credit for.

Speculative positioning is light. The US Portfolio Strategy sentiment indicator, a positioning meter, has been negative for six consecutive weeks. Net exposure across the GS global prime book is in the 10th percentile of the past year, and the US market has been net sold for three straight weeks.

The S&P broke out last week but a client turnover measure ranked 49th of the past 52 weeks. The desk says it cannot remember a market at highs attracting so little chase, and expects net positive flows through year-end, helped by the start of earnings season.

A GS corporate supply and demand note for 2027 forecasts $600bn of primary issuance, including $175bn of IPOs. That is under 1% of US equity market cap, in line with the long-term average. Buybacks plus M&A should total $2tr.

Lockup expirations could add $1.7tr of equity supply. Combined with the $600bn of issuance, net US equity supply could rise the most since 2000. The desk flags the lockup figure as a wildcard that is still to be determined.

Directional view: the tactical setup is net positive and the technicals should improve through October and past the midterms. The desk's instinct is that 2027 is setting up as a complicated year, citing the supply picture and a broad deceleration in earnings growth.
Short-term plan: stay short fixed income, stay long NDX, TPX and GSCI.

Since the March 2009 lows the S&P is up 16-fold in total returns, with exactly one recession of about two months. U-M consumer sentiment is nonetheless lower than in March 2009 and just printed its second lowest reading on record in a series back to 1952. The desk finds this disjunction striking and attributes the mood to inflation and news-flow worries.
earnings_insights: Earnings season is expected to support equity flows, per the desk. Pasquariello also cites a broad deceleration of earnings growth as a reason 2027 may be complicated.

tension_points.bull_case: Major US indices are up double digits YTD, all but two S&P sectors are higher, nearly 2-in-3 names are positive, and 123 names are up 25% or more versus 42 down 25% or more.
tension_points.bear_case: The S&P is highly concentrated, and the median stock is 15% below its 52-week high, the worst reading since the dot-com bubble. Investors who missed mega cap tech missed a lot.

tension_points.bull_case: Tactical setup is net positive into the midterms, positioning is light, and buybacks plus M&A of $2tr offset $600bn of issuance.
tension_points.bear_case: Lockup expirations of up to $1.7tr plus $600bn of issuance could make net US equity supply the largest increase since 2000, alongside slowing earnings growth.
